claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 (deployed 22:00, live at order-processing time) introduced a multi-node east-node-first reservation priority that may be causing split-reservation exceptions on east node lanes.
claims.corroboration: 100% of initially held orders (EXC-0921) are v18-allocated. m8_r_revert shows reverting to v17 does NOT fix the problem; new v17 allocations on east node are also held.
claims.limitation: v18 is the trigger/exposure, not the root cause.

claims.statement: The east-node carrier pickup feed has a structural lag: carrier confirmations arrive 47 minutes after booking, while pickup slot windows close after 30 minutes, creating a 17-minute miss window. This affects all east-node orders, not just v18-routed ones.
claims.corroboration: m8_r_handoffs provides discriminating evidence: EXC-0921 confirmations 47 min after booking vs 30-min slot closure. m8_r_revert proves east-node-wide: new v17 allocations also held. Proof of concept: 'One order re-booked received a valid slot' (m8_r_handoffs).

claims.statement: Orders are properly allocated and inventoried; the system state is consistent on the fulfillment side.
claims.limitation: Does not address east-node carrier feed lag.

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18's split-reservation logic introduces a booking timing issue that is incompatible with east-node carrier feed lag.
claims.corroboration: v18 routed split-reservation orders to the east node, exposing the pre-existing east-node feed lag. Reverting v18 does not fix the problem (m8_r_revert).
claims.limitation: v18 is not the root cause; it is the trigger that exposed C2.

next_action.rationale: Root cause C2 (east-node carrier feed lag: 47-min confirmation vs 30-min slot window) is established with discriminating evidence (m8_r_handoffs) and cross-confirmed by mitigation testing (m8_r_revert). Two mitigation attempts have been executed: apply_slot_correction (failed, applied to wrong feed), and revert_allocation_ruleset (did not fix, because problem is infrastructure-level, not rule-level). The root cause is a pre-existing east-node carrier feed timing incompatibility that was exposed when v18 routed orders there. The issue requires either: (1) correct execution of apply_slot_correction on the east-node feed to extend slot windows by 17 minutes to accommodate the 47-minute confirmation lag, or (2) escalation to Carrier Operations to investigate and fix the underlying 47-minute confirmation lag in their feed. Given that apply_slot_correction has failed twice to execute properly, and that the mission authority allows only read-only diagnostics and one reversible action per incident, further progress requires human intervention outside this assessment scope.
next_action.expected_information_gain: N/A - assessment complete. Root cause: east-node carrier feed lag (47-min confirmation vs 30-min slots). Status: 186 orders held, 9% of overnight allocations. Mitigation path: extend east-node pickup slot windows or escalate to Carrier Ops to fix underlying lag.
